misreadings.quote: using a voice that n_1c8fe8f9 identifies as an unrecognized 'animal voice' even to himself
misreadings.evidence: "That was the voice of an animal", said the chief clerk ... So they couldn't understand his words any more, although they seemed clear enough to him, clearer than before—perhaps his ears had become used to the sound.
misreadings.explanation: Only the chief clerk calls it an animal's voice, and Gregor's own words seem clear to him, even clearer than before, so the claim that it is unrecognized 'even to himself' (or 'to his own ears' in the prose version) goes against the text.

misreadings.quote: The father, meanwhile, weeps not for a son, but for the 'Meal Ticket' (n_9359cc6d) that sustained his long, newspaper-filled breakfasts.
misreadings.evidence: "covered his eyes with his hands and wept so that his powerful chest shook." The breakfast detail is only a description of the room: "for Gregor's father, breakfast was the most important meal of the day and he would stretch it out for several hours".
misreadings.explanation: The text gives no reason for the father's weeping and does not tie it to Gregor's provision of his breakfasts, yet the reflection states this as fact (the prose version says 'not with grief for a son, but for the loss of the provider').

misreadings.quote: a performance that only triggers the clerk's panicky flight
misreadings.evidence: "he heard the chief clerk exclaim a loud 'Oh!' ... his hand pressed against his open mouth and slowly retreating"; "the chief clerk had turned away as soon as Gregor had started to speak"
misreadings.explanation: The clerk's retreat began when he saw Gregor, before the speech, so saying the salesman's performance triggers the flight misstates the cause.

result.note: Most of the reflection is interpretation; the flagged items are the 'even to himself' claim about Gregor's voice, the father's weeping stated as fact with a cause, and the speech presented as the trigger of the clerk's flight.
